bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (kernel input devices), springboard/src/media/v4l2.rs (UVC cameras via kernel V4L2), springboard/audiod (audio devices); no app-facing USB API; springboard/sdk/src/usb_device.rs (claim planning, not sent to devices)
summary: IOUSBHost is Apple's framework for user-space host-mode USB drivers that let apps talk to custom USB devices. BifrOSt has no app-facing USB transport API: the Linux kernel drives USB, and the shell and daemons handle input, camera and audio devices by class. Raw device claim, descriptors, pipes and isochronous streams have no SDK counterpart, and the app sandbox does not expose USB device nodes.

features.feature: Device driver access (claim, configure, descriptors, device requests)
features.note: An app can plan a claim (configuration and alternate-setting requests in order, and the pipes the interface opens), and the setup packets and descriptors are encoded and parsed in the inline tests of usb_claim.rs and usb_descriptors.rs. Gap: nothing sends the requests and the sandbox binds no /dev/bus/usb, which needs hardware and a Midget check. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/core/src/usb_claim.rs; tests usb_claim::tests.

Wave 5 (w5-iousbhost, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests, now including can_print (a printer interface needs a bulk-out endpoint) and the printer name for a list, tested headless in parity_sdk-complete-45.rs. Not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The print API does not expose a USB transport. No scanner API exists: most USB scanners use vendor-specific protocols, so scanner support needs per-model drivers and a device. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/core/src/usb_printer.rs; tests usb_printer::tests.

features.feature: Host controller interface and state machines (hubs, controller, port, endpoint)
features.bifrost: Linux kernel xHCI and USB stack
features.note: Controller-side DriverKit plumbing. On Linux the kernel owns it, and a desktop app has no use for it.

features.feature: Error domain and structures, enumerations, constants
features.note: Apple error and ABI types for the IOKit USB path. No equivalent is needed without the framework.

gaps: No app-facing transport: the claim plan (springboard/sdk/src/usb_device.rs) is not sent and no control, bulk, interrupt or isochronous request reaches a device (IOUSBHostDevice, IOUSBHostInterface, IOUSBHostPipe, IOUSBHostStream).
The app sandbox (springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs) does not bind USB device nodes, so a sandboxed app cannot reach raw USB even if an API existed.
No USB transport for printers (springboard/ui/src/print.rs); scanner sessions are an SDK model (sdk scan_session.rs) with no transport.

Owner decision needed: whether a desktop needs app-level raw USB access at all. The triage note says likely n/a; the framework's stated use cases (cameras, audio, scanners, printers, MIDI, hubs) are mostly covered at the system layer, which leaves custom device drivers as the real gap.
